artist.artist_description: Hank Snow was a Canadian country music artist born in 1914 in Nova Scotia. He began his career performing on local radio stations and rose to fame with hits like "I'm Moving On," which became a number one hit in the U.S. Snow was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1979 and was known for his yodeling and his signature song "The Golden Rocket."

Simon & Garfunkel are an American folk-rock duo formed in 1957 by Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel, who met in high school in Queens, New York. They achieved international fame with hits like "The Sound of Silence" and "Bridge Over Troubled Water," the latter earning them six Grammy Awards in 1971. A lesser-known fact is that they initially performed under the name Tom & Jerry before adopting Simon & Garfunkel.
